findings.body: The returned monitor context contains the raw config with the numeric `schedule_type` value instead of the humanized display value computed just above, so the issue event's monitor context shows an unreadable integer; the local `config` variable is dead code.
findings.failure_mode: Issue occurrence payload carries an un-humanized schedule_type and the surrounding copy/mutation code is unreachable in effect.
findings.impact: The returned monitor context contains the raw config with the numeric `schedule_type` value instead of the humanized display value computed just above, so the issue event's monitor context shows an unreadable integer; the local `config` variable is dead code.
findings.root_cause: The new module builds a modified copy of the config into a local `config` variable but the returned mapping still references `monitor_environment.monitor.config`, leaving the copy unused.
findings.suggested_fix: Return the mutated copy, i.e. use `"config": config,` in the returned dictionary of `get_monitor_environment_context`.
findings.title: get_monitor_environment_context discards humanized schedule_type copy
findings.trigger: Any monitor incident occurrence produced for a monitor whose config contains a `schedule_type` key (all crontab/interval monitors) reaches `get_monitor_environment_context` while building the `contexts.monitor` payload.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 168 verbatim shows `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config,` while lines 160-162 create a local `config` copy with humanized `schedule_type`. The patch introduces this discrepancy: the mutated copy is never used, so the returned context contains the raw numeric value instead of the display string.
